title: Another season of over firing and burning brain (2)
text:
The knee and thigh long sweater I wore over my top dress on 2 September did not warm me up enough against the barometric cold of this rain season as did
The knee and thigh long sweater I wore over my top dress on 2 September did not warm me up enough against the barometric cold of this rain season as did the eruptions in Abuja of Nyesom Wike, the Federal Capital Territory Minister.
Fear of the political unknown is a major cause of misfiring, overfiring and burning brains in this, as in any election season. In the first part of this series, I explained how a tumultuous season such as this one may cause free radical molecules in the brain to impact as many as one million holes in a single brain cell everyday.
This impact may cause such a cell to leak, lose energy, prematurely age, die or predispose anyone to challenges of an unbalanced brain, unless those leaks are promptly sealed by anti-oxidants. Unfortunately, not every one of us eat well enough to give our bodies the materials for producing these anti-oxidants. And that is why, in this season and the ones to follow, we may find more persons misbehaving at home, in public places and in the streets.
Wike said if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu lost the election next year, the victor, Atiku Abubakar or Peter Obi, would make political and perhaps, legal mince meat of him. Wike overspeaks. Shall we say he is talkative? Talkatives always leave crevices in their mud castles through which lizards and other rodents, enemies of the household, may rivet indoors.
His speech must be making many brains in the Presidency to be overfiring, if not burning already. Can it not be that fear of vulnerability to political reprisals make Wike a bewildering politician who keeps a visible leg in his own party, the PDP, and a shadow leg in the President’s ruling APC? Year 2031 may be the upcoming season which has been making Wike to be misfiring, over-firing and burning.
What if the APC does not value him in 2031, and the PDP at that time wants a Northerner as President? Couldn’t Wike fill the bill as Vice-President on PDP ticket? If APC values him, but goes for a Northerner as President, and PDP meanwhile has gone down, couldn’t he become Vice- President on APC ticket? These questions must be keeping several heads awake across the political chess board!
Wike may not over heat the brain for long, nevertheless, as Peter Obi and the Obedients Movement now appear able to, whenever Obi’s campaign machinery runs into any barricade. It once happened in Edo State. It has happened again in Benue State. This time, Obi was going to Benue to visit a community where killings had just taken place.
His campaign team was sent back by angry youths. The Governor, Hyacinth Alia, said Obi did not inform him he was coming,so he could arrange special security for the visitors. Obi’s people said they informed the Police Headquarters in Abuja. The police confirmed the arrest of 24 youths suspected to be among the crowd which sent Obi back.
The event has raised fundamental constitutional questions which are wracking the head. In the midst of it all, history is not asleep. Many persons have reffered to a similar event in Anambra State when Obi was Governor. Senator Chris Ngige was seeking election as Governor.
A powerful APC delegation arrived in Anambra to support his campaign. The “powers that be” restricted the delegation to hotel rooms. Obi said he had no hand in it. Some persons said it was the decision of police headquarters in Abuja.
Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was Nigeria’s President and in charge of the Federal Police. In 2015 he would be defeated by a multi-headed APC and yield ground to Mohammadu Buhari. When Peter Obi went to Kaduna State 10 years after in 2023 to campaign for the Presidency, host Governor El Rufia revisited the Anambra detentions of 2013. This was during a courtesy visit by Obi and his team to host Governor El Rufia and some Northerner leaders.
“In 2013, I went to Anambra State as an official of the APC to witness the bye-election for governorship. Your next guest, Peter Obi, as Governor, got me arrested and detained for 48 hours in my hotel room. Now I’m the Governor of Kaduna State and he’s coming to Kaduna…but we are Northerners. We are civilised.
We do not do things like that. ” I cannot imagine what would have happened if El Rufia frontally blocked Peter Obi in retaliation, although Obi claimed he knew nothing about what happen to the APC delegation. El Rufia was in Anambra as APC National Deputy Secretary. In 2023, El Rufia said…“three SSS officers with AK-47… have directive from Abuja to restrict me to my room”.
In a Follow up court case, Justice Bature Gafai found the “SSS liable” for unlawful detention and ordered them to pay N2M damages plus apology. The judgment did not mentioned Peter Obi or Anambra government as culprits.
“There’s no way I can do that… I never ordered any AIG to arrest or detain anybody”. Nevertheless, an albatross of Anambra 2013 detention still hangs around Peter Obi. Many persons refer to it when he encounters campaign blockages, and he tries to politically profit from them. Making storms in tea cups may be his own campaign strategy to which he is entitled, but it rattles the election atmospsphere and can triger emotional mayhem.
Many persons where still sorrowful in Benue State where killings had not abated. Governor Hyacinth Alia, a Catholic Priest, was the Chief mourner of his people, politics aside. If spiritually, that is inwardly, genuinely and not intellectually, cunning, and outwardly, Peter Obi was going to mourn with Benue people, and not to fish in troubled political waters, his first port of call ought to have been the Governor and, after him, the traditional ruler of the disturbed communities.
By his own admission, Peter Obi informed only the police headquarters in Abuja, sidelining the government and traditional authorities. It is still unclear why the youths opposed his visit. Did they assume he was coming to make political capital of the sorrow in their land? Emotionally Obi’s linguistic followers have warned that nothing must happen to him.
Emotionally, too, many persons blamed the Governor for saying Peter Obi did not inform him of the visit. True, citizens are not legally bound to obtain a Governor consent to come to town.
However, some citizens are weightier security risks than others. Obi as a Presidential candidate is an untouchable in this emotional and dangerous season. That is what the Governor is saying. If he has ideas superior to the ones on the Nigerian table right now, he should state them clearly and explain a step-by step strategy for achieving them.
Many Nigerians have poor emotional intelligence. They cannot see deep down to the bottom of a whirlpool. They can burn the Nation. In this second part of the series, I will not jump the gun or beat the queue as I did in the first part to immediately present information on the herbs I listed then as useful for this season of misfiring, over-firing and burning brains.
This season of unreason and unintelligent emotions may mangle or damage not only the brain, but, also, the heart, the nerves or even the kidneys. In lucky persons, the damage may be reversible, but irreversible in unlucky ones. PDP defends Wike’s support for Tinubu Please forgive me that I forgot to mention an important nerve herb in the first part of the series. It is called LION’S MANE MUSHROOM.
A young Italian medical doctor discovered its healing influence on damaged nerves during the second World War when she was experimenting with plant medicines which may repair and revive mangled or damaged nerves. Barred from university on racial grounds, Dr Rita Levi-Montalcini carried out the studies in her Turin flat. She worked on damaged chicken embryos and discovered extracts in LION’S MANE MUSHROOM which repaired the mangled nerves.
This was the birth of Nerve Growth Factor also called Nerve growth hormone for which she won a Nobel Prize in 1986. It is a protein made by the body to help brain cell to grow and survive. Her experiments were intriguing, because war planes were flying over her neighbourhood and the fear of bombs dropping on her room which was her laboratory did not overcome her goal.
After her, other studies have unveiled LION’S MANE Mushroom’s usefulness in other health including CANCER. I mentioned LION’S MANE MUSHROOM for the use of anyone who may encounter nervous breakdowns in this political campaign season. We must now hurriedly return to desperation for power as a major cause of the season’s political tensions in which many person’s may drop dead or fall seriously ill or sick. No fewer than 38 persons died in Osun state last month over political disputes.
Earthly remains of some of them may not have been interred before the winner and the loser opnely sheathed their swords, promising to work together in the on-going Presidential campaigns. Similarly, several opposition parties under the umbrella term G-100 are planning to develop a stronger and mightier fighting force against the giant APC. They are encouraged by the APC, similarly formed from smaller parties which individually were nothing but preys for the then mighty PDP.
They may not remember a secret of the APC gel. This was that the largest of the fringe parties yielded the Presidency to a smaller one. In the opposition of today, only the ADC of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the NDC of Peter Obi have some muscles to flex and teeth to bite. The fringe parties of the proposed OPPOSITION COALITION are seeking a UNIFIED CANDIDACY.
Atiku and Obi have said they would not yield way for each other. Luckily for Atiku, his eligibility to run may no longer depend on a supreme court proclamation. I used to wonder what the opposition landscape would be like if the supreme court said he was ineligible. Would Obi have wished that Atiku was knocked out?
He has not stopped claiming that he won the 2023 polls in which he trailed third after Tinubu and Atiku. Isn’t he,thereby, fuelling negative emotions and undermining the judiciary and peace in the land? If Atiku’s fate depended on the supreme court and he was knocked out, the opposition coalition may misfire or overfire, linking his fate to the handiwork of President Tinubu. Atiku could be like a python attacked in its tail, a very violent and poisonous snake.
The future of Atiku would be a major concern for the President. Peter Obi would pretend to back him up with eyes and heart, discreetly hoping, however, on the inheritance of Atiku’s political estate. Together, they would sing songs that the Presidency has pocketed the judiciary. Didn’t they say something similar to that when the EFCC froze the bank account of Osun state government during last month’s Governorship elections?
A few months before then, huge sums had been exiting the accounts for destinations allegedly outside their statutory allocations. Osun government alleged that the hands of Esau were at play. To remedy his image as an impassioned onlooker, the President openly put EFCC on hold, a measure some accountability apostle and disciples have described as a dangerous interference with due process. But what could he have done?
If the EFCC was recalcitrant, and the Governor lost, It is possible killings would still be going on, and the state would have over stretched Nigeria’s already inflamed population. Rabiu Kwankwaso knows why he is asking Atiku to go as a sacrifice for the Opposition to win. Obi has no serious political structures. Even Kwankwaso’s in only Kano state may be outdated.
If Obi yields to run with Atiku, Kwankwaso will be a loser. If Atiku is pressured to go, Kwankwaso may inherit Atiku’s structure in the North to handcuff Obi’s Presidency for a win. They are strange bed fellows pretending to not be cat and mouse till they become President and Vice-President. What do I mean?
Both men are rooted in ETHNIC POLITICS. I am not saying it is bad for a politician to be a lover of his people. Charity begins from home.. What I am saying is that, when his people and others collide, which is inevitable in a plural ethnic country, the politicians should be able to look at his people straight in the face, irrespective of their votes, and tell them they are wrong, if, indeed, they are.
I take my bearing from when Obi was Governor of Anambra state and from the 2023 General elections, among others. As Anambra Governor, Obi once send home some Northerners as persona nongrata. Pronto, Kwakwanso hit Anambra for explanation. In the 2023 General elections, a video went viral in which Senator Ibikunle Amosu interviewed Kassim Shettima, now Vice-President.
In that interview, Shettima said Kankwaso was the choice of Northerners for President in 2015, not Muhammadu Buhari. Shititima told Amosu that Northerners believed Kankwaso would rescue their informal economy from South-easterners and empower Northerners to acquire management skills in this terrain which included motor mechanic workshops and patent medicine stores, among others.
I would like to recall, also, Obi’s dash to Lagos to request of the Governor explanations for the closure of the LADIPO street motor vehicles spare parts market over degradation of the Mushin environment. The market had been found to be terribly overcrowded, partially turned into housing residencies against the law, polluting the canal behind it, pasting the road adjourning it with grease, black engine oil and blocking roads.
At that time several markets in Lagos were shut for lesser infactions. Recently, Obi has been over active in Lagos affairs, questioning positions of the government in matters which involve “ his people” and the state. Such a case was that of the ownership of a property in Ikeja GRA, Lagos.
Nevertheless, Obi may lose ground in his linguistic territory on 15 September 2026, Mazi, news analyst for Jordan Fm radio station told Oreoluwa Ogunsholu on TALKING POINT programme, the Opposition may profit from Peter Obi steping down for Atiku Abubakar. Was he flying a kite? Politicians will seek to make small minds of all of us, if we let them. The Universe is a huge mind.
It does not nurture small minds and that is why small minds wither. Literally, Atiku and Obi have been saying for years that Tinubu has been sleeping and snoring in the Presidential Villa. That was why, last week, I recalled from my publication several ongoing projects on which the Tinubu Administration has been spending money for more than three years. Today, I would gladly mention two more which many persons believe are good for the economy.
This is to run from Lagos to Maiduguri at about 330 kilometres per hour, and take the travelers from Lagos to Abuja only three hours. Another is to run from Kaduna to Kano. They are different from the Lagos-Calabar super highway and the Lagos-Sokoto super highway proposed by the Shagari Presidency in 1979, that is 47 years ago! In four years, a President is doing what several Presidents, including military rulers, couldn’t do in 47 years!
Isn’t that commendable? Only small minds would think otherwise. In 2015, this column in about 13 articles, published by the NATION Newspaper and posted on facebook at JOHN OLUFEMI KUSA, advised President Ebele Jonathan and challenger Muhammadu Buhari to build railways across the country as a means of opening it up, stimulating economic growth and creating jobs. Railways are among what made Malaysia a miracle country today.
In colonial Nigeria, Nigeria Railway Corporation was the biggest employer and opened the country up for economic growth. With trains now to move from Lagos to Maiduguri, from Lagos to Calabar, from Badagry to Lagos, from Lagos to Kaduna , from Sokoto to Maiduguri, would food crops and goods not move faster and cheaper? Will rail transportation not offer many jobs? Is the investment foolish spending?
Why are supposedly intelligent persons behaving like beer parlour rustics? Are they inwardly, psychically or spiritually slumbering or sleeping, seeing but not comprehending, and merely LUSTING for power? Please do not get me wrong. I am not saying that the President is ALL-WISE and Atiku and Obi ALL-FOOL.
What I am saying is they should not BERATE for the sake of BERATING. They can tell me the President has tried, even list his achievements, and then say there is still a lot more to do, mention them and state how they are to be done,within the limits of present resources and natural income.
When, in 1979, Chief Obafemi Awolowo proposed free education at all levels, he told us how much money Federal Civil Servants were spending everyday on tea, groundnut and biscuits, as refreshments in their offices. He said this was enough to foot the bill. General Olusegun Obasanjo’s government could not deny this wastage in his Administration.
